WSGI Runtime, Contexts, and Dispatch Engine
Section: Dispatch and routing
The concrete Flask request path from a WSGI environ through context binding, routing, handlers, response finalization, teardown, and signals. Explains contextvars-backed proxies, exception paths, and how ensure_sync runs async handlers without turning Flask into an ASGI runtime.
Class-based views are an extension point within this same dispatch path, not a second runtime. View.as view creates the registered function, optionally instantiates a view per request, and calls dispatch request ; MethodView selects the method named by the HTTP verb and falls back from HEAD to GET . Both use current app.ensure sync ( views.py , views.py ).

End-to-End Request and Response Workflow
Section: Session ownership and extension points
Traces how Flask turns a WSGI environ into a response, including context and session setup, routing, preprocessing, dispatch, finalization, persistence, signals, and teardown. Separates routing failures, handled and unhandled exceptions, and failures while finalizing or iterating a response.
RequestContext.push calls the configured session interface.open session once for the first push. If it returns None , Flask creates the interface's null session; null sessions are not saved. The default SecureCookieSessionInterface loads a signed cookie using secret key , treats a missing or invalid cookie as a new session, and writes or deletes the cookie according to access and modification state. A session may be read by URL converters, handlers, and response hooks, but it is persisted only in process response after response hooks have run.
